messages:
Devon: ran perf sweep on main after #3421. Short-seq p50 up 5-12% when selector chooses "wide" vectorized kernels.

Maria: saw same in nightly. Mostly seq_len <= 32, batch sizes 1-3. p95 unchanged.

Chris: profile? flamegraph or nvprof helps to see if it's launch overhead vs compute.

Devon: uploaded flame.svg. Key spots from perf sampling:
- CPU: time in launch/queue sync
- GPU: tiny kernels (microsec) so launch latency dominates

perf-bot: perf/regression alert job=nightly/main-tune-2026-03-15 delta_p50=+8% trace=perf-176950

Vikram: my take: selector prefers wide kernels because they win when batches are larger, but for small batches and short seq the launch+KV penalties tip it negative.

Maria: KV layout differences between paths cause extra memcpy and CPU-side invalidation when switching paths mid-run.

Chris: If kernel time <100us and launch ~30-60us it's material. Our scheduler dispatch policy sends immediately to protect tail latency, which prevents batching amortization.

Devon: repro steps:
1) model=meta-7b
2) seq=16
3) concurrent clients=2
4) batch_policy=immediate
Run: ./tools/trace_spawn.sh --id=176950

Maria: local hack: force narrow kernel when seq<=32 && batch<=3. Restores p50 but may hurt throughput for batchy traffic.

Vikram: we should build a cost-aware selector: estimate launch + exec(batch,seq) + kv_penalty. Inputs: observed batch histogram, seq dist, kv_hit_rate, kernel_exec_estimates.

Chris: collect live signals: batch_size histograms, observed kernel durations, kv miss counters. Lightweight tuner updates thresholds every few minutes.

Devon: plan:
- hotfix: prefer narrow for seq<=32 & batch<=3 (branch perf/urgent/execpath-shortseq)
- mid: telemetry + cost model in selector
- long: change continuous batching to allow small waits when beneficial

Maria: continuous batching adds waiting decisions; a 5-10ms wait might help amortize but violates some strict SLOs.

Vikram: add per-route policy: strict-latency vs throughput-optimized. Selector consults route.

perf-bot: note: job #176940 on a100-80gb recorded launch=48us; older GPUs worse.

Chris: impl notes:
- expose kernel_estimates: {"narrow": "lat_us_by_seq...", "wide": "..."}
- selector reads batch_histogram + avg_kv_miss
- fallback: if wide chosen but latency exceeds threshold 3x, force narrow for next N inferences (cooldown)

Devon: need to ignore warmup samples after model swap, warmup skews autotune.

Maria: add warmup window per model version (first M tokens ignored).

Vikram: I'll draft PR for cost model and telemetry schema. assigning perf/176950-tuner to me.

Devon: I'll open hotfix PR and run canary.

Chris: infra, canary to dedicated pool to gather signals? @infra-bot

infra-bot: scheduled canary: pool=canary-runtime-2 start=2026-03-16T22:00Z notify=#eng-runtime

Maria: actions:
- Devon: hotfix PR
- Vikram: telemetry & cost-model PR
- Chris: cooldown & warmup logic
- Devon/Maria: run canary and paste perf diffs

Devon: will post results. :white_check_mark:

Chris: add "selector_switches" counter to logs to track path flips.

Maria: add short doc in docs/runtime/exec-selector.md describing knobs.

Vikram: link to draft: https://go.redwood/notes/exec-path-cost-model

Devon: end thread — ping if canary shows surprises.
